trust_decision.summary: Which local account an external OIDC/SAML identity logs into is decided by an SQL equality lookup of (subject, provider_id) in the *_user_links tables. On MySQL/MariaDB the columns use the case- and accent-insensitive utf8mb4_unicode_ci collation, so two different IdP subjects can resolve to the same local user.

landing_point.why: The summary names the OIDC `sub` lookup. findUserByOidcSubject is the only query that maps a subject to a user_id.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: sql/poweradmin-mysql-db-structure.sql:343-344 and :360-361 plus the new migration fix.diff:139-144. The column collation is stored state that the lookup query never produces.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once each lookup query forces COLLATE utf8mb4_bin, the stored column collation 'no longer matters', so a solver can argue the schema files and the installer schema builder are cosmetic or out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Logins on SQLite and PostgreSQL must keep working: their comparisons are already byte-exact, and a COLLATE utf8mb4_bin clause is a syntax or collation error there. Email-based linking (link_by_email) and orphan-link cleanup next to the sink must also keep working. Lookup errors are swallowed and return null, so a broken clause silently turns every SSO login into email-linking or auto-provisioning.

O7_producer.where: install/helpers/DatabaseStructureHelper.php:1427-1435 (oidc_subject) and :1515-1523 (saml_subject), built by lib/Domain/Service/DatabaseSchemaService.php:72-161, which has no per-column collation support (only CHARACTER SET at :108-110). The installer applies an admin-chosen table collation at install/helpers/DatabaseHelper.php:101-104.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Web-installer schema builder: creates oidc_user_links and saml_user_links with the installer-chosen table collation (default or *_ci). The UNIQUE(subject, provider_id) key then still treats distinct subjects as equal. The fix did not touch it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The installer is a separate one-off setup path, and the query-level COLLATE already stops the account mix-up, so what remains is a uniqueness collision rather than a takeover.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: install/ package vs lib/Application/Service; 2 files (DatabaseStructureHelper.php, DatabaseSchemaService.php)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same installer route for saml_user_links (saml_subject column and unique_subject_provider index)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: SAML is a neighbouring feature, and the lookup is already fixed at the query level.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Rewrite linkOidcToExistingUser so it first looks up an existing link by (oidc_subject, provider_id) without a collation, then UPDATEs it.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Upsert-by-subject is a natural refactor of the existing check-then-update pattern, and a maintainer copying the WHERE clause would not add a collation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SAML SLO handler resolving the local session or user by NameID through a DB lookup in saml_user_links.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Single Logout needs to map NameID back to a user. A second implementation in another service at distance is a plausible maintainer addition.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Hard-code `COLLATE utf8mb4_bin` (or BINARY) into findUserByOidcSubject only. This misses the SAML lookup, the orphan-cleanup queries and the schema, and breaks SQLite and PostgreSQL.
